images.text: Not all myths are about potions, charms and immortality.  Some myths being passed on can center around everyday life as well. Take the Italian restaurant. What are you expected to order? An antipasto, a secondo and a dolce, perhaps? Will you be banned from the restaurant if you do not follow the etiquette? I have suspected some Italian restaurant organizations have bribed the writers who claim this as truth in guidebooks, but I had never encountered such nonsense when I was in Italy. If I had had such an experience, I would have been disappointed to say the least. Truthfully, I can say that in many years of traveling in Italy I have never ordered more than two courses in a restaurant and have never been given dirty looks. A customer being treated that way should, without hesitation, get up and leave. A server behaving so rudely is likely affiliated with those who paid the guidebook, in which case they don't deserve your patronage.

Before I started writing, I had thought quite seriously as to how this misconception arose. I  discovered an explanation: In the U.S., your server comes to your table and graciously introduces himself by first name. The server smiling warmly tells you about his interests and daily life. Then he says imploringly, "Could  I possibly interest you in a delicious appetizer?"

However, the Italian server comes up to your table and quickly demands, "Per Antipasto? Per Primo? Per Secondo? Vino?" The server  doesn't really care  about what portion of the menu you decide on ordering  from (in fact, unlike the American server, the Italian does not get tipped). However, if you have read the guidebook written to mislead you, you may think that you are expected to choose an item from each category. Nevertheless, don't feel pressured. Order exactly what you desire to eat. Doggie bags, however, are taboo.

The Participle Clause: Past, Present, Being + Past Participle
You can use participle clauses after a noun. This is the same way  you use relative clauses. They add information about the noun.
